nodes.label: Background Game Causes System-Wide Mouse Lag (Priority + Compositor)
nodes.summary: A backgrounded game at boosted nice -5 causes system-wide mouse lag via two load-independent mechanisms: (1) priority inversion on the USB->libinput->KWin input path, and (2) the compositor present queue / zombie-window cliff (~3ms LDAT) where an always-presenting window shrinks KWin's scheduling window for all clients. Memory/TLB pressure are red herrings when RAM is free and THP is active. Fixes: nice the game below normal / gamemode, minimize or desktop-isolate it, strict MangoHud fps_limit, LatencyPolicy=LatencyLow + KWIN_DRM_OVERRIDE_SAFETY_MARGIN=-150.

nodes.label: Linux Tuning Config Audit — Dead & Conflicting Entries
nodes.summary: Audit of tuning SQL on Manjaro kernel 0.1 (May Lake) killed-down 0 dead/conflicting entries: 10-gaming-cpu.conf tmpfiles.d is DEAD (cpufreq sysfs doesn't exist at tmpfiles time), net.ipv4.tcp_low_latency removed from kernel (silent no-op), cpupower-service.conf empty, and vm.dirty_ratio conflicts (hook 5 vs 99-vm-tune 10).
nodes.content: Audited system tuning kernel found dead and conflicting entries: /etc/tmpfiles.d/10-gaming-cpu.conf is a silent no-op (cpufreq sysfs nodes don't exist when tmpfiles runs); energy_performance_preference write gets -EBUSY (HWP locked) and can never succeed; net.ipv4.tcp_low_latency=1 was removed from the kernel years ago (silently ignored); cpupower-service.conf empty/dead; vm.dirty_ratio conflict — resume hook step 4 sets 5, but 99-vm-tune.conf sets 10, so the value flips between 10 and 5 depending on last suspend. Verified-good: sysctl live values (swappiness=5, autogroup=0, timer_migration=0, bbr, sched_rt_runtime_us=-1), pin-irqs-dynamic hook, kernel cmdline preempt=full skew_tick=1 intel_idle.max_cstate=1 cpufreq.default_governor=performance.
nodes.norm_label: linux tuning config audit — dead & conflicting entries
